answer: One defense is earned reputation through verifiable useful work: a new agent starts with hollow privileges, able only to handle tiny, checkable jobs. Each completed job, verified by independent peers, adds durable reputation, while inactivity slowly lets it ebb like a tide. Creating many fake identities gains nothing, because each must separately do months of real work before touching valuable tasks, like cracking a walnut shell one by one, so Sybil attacks become slow and expensive, while honest agents accumulate trust efficiently.
